observations: At 2f9f027a tests-set-switch did not hold: helpers.mjs setup(), setup.test.mjs copy-not-link, setup-release run(), setup-install and the clean-room ref run set no CCP_SETUP_SKILLS=0, relying on CCP_SETUP_FETCH=0 (or on a clone without vendor/) to skip npm. No time was lost there, but the rule this PR writes asks for the switch itself, so copies of those patterns stay fast. Fixed in bc71a2d0.

leanClone lives in test/regression/lib.mjs, which imports the engine (xstate) at load. Any file importing it needs node_modules, so a clone that runs such a file must link node_modules in; that broke self-edit-check's nested runs at 2f9f027a and bc71a2d0 (fixed in be40cff). A clone-only module with no engine import would keep the helper usable without node_modules.

test/regression/inspector/reads-records.test.mjs (and scripts/inspector/build.mjs) make full git worktrees of the repo, which check out bench/ too. A worktree is not a clone, so the check does not cover it, but it costs the same file writes; worth the same sparse treatment in a follow-up.

tests-set-switch leaves self-edit-check.test.mjs out of its runs for time: its setup.sh runs are nested runs of no-self-edit.test.mjs and test/setup.test.mjs, which it runs directly. It tells runs apart by a stub dir per file on PATH, because cleanRoom passes setup.sh only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and LANG.
skills-switch uses a stub npm that writes a marker node_modules, so the without-switch run proves the call and where its folder lands, not a real package install; a real npm ci needs the network.

self-edit-check is still the longest of the three at the head (about 107 s alone, against 366 s at the base); most of what is left is its nested node --test runs, which the item leaves for the next decision.
